title: What If Your AI Agent Had A Dozen Helpers?
sources: Diane Sarkis, 'Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop', Claude (claude.com), Oct 22 2026: https://claude.com/resources/articles/building-agents-when-to-fold-subagents-into-your-main-agent-loop (a company with about a dozen specialist subagents; details get lost in handoffs, a 'telephone game'; start evals with ~10 golden examples; fold subagents in one at a time, prompts become skills that load only when needed; run each task more than once; keep a subagent only if the folded version scores worse; one customer saw roughly 2x faster runtime with a single agent loop)

lines.text: What would you do if your AI agent had a dozen helpers,
lines.caps: What would *you do | if your *agent | had a *dozen helpers,

lines.text: and it still felt slow and kind of confused?
lines.caps: it still felt *slow | and kind of *confused?

lines.text: Well, every handoff is like a game of telephone,
where little details get lost along the way.
Step one: build a small test set first, even ten real examples.
lines.caps: Step *one: | build a small *test set | even *ten real examples.

lines.text: Step two: fold one helper back into the main agent,
lines.caps: Step *two: | fold *one helper | into the *main agent,

lines.text: turning its prompt into a skill that loads only when needed.
lines.caps: its prompt into a *skill | that *loads | only when *needed.

lines.text: Step three: run your tests again, more than once,
lines.caps: Step *three: | run your *tests again, | more than *once,

lines.text: and keep the helper only if the folded version scores worse.
lines.caps: keep the *helper | only if the *folded version | scores *worse.

lines.text: One team tried this and got about two times faster.
So one brain, one memory, the right tools,
and maybe your agent never needed all those helpers.
